notes: Parts are unchanged from step 1. All parts are in the catalogue, so no new part types were needed.
The image shows five wires (red, black, teal, orange, short black). The text names only three, so the orange and short black wires come from the image.

Circuit: 5V goes to the + rail (tp), GND goes to the - rail (tn). Pin 2 and the 10k pull-down resistor share the same button side (column 6, 't' half). The other button side (4b/6b) connects through the orange wire to the + rail.

The image has the button's two legs in the same column joined (vertical pair). The catalogue card puts the joined pairs 1.l/1.r on one half and 2.l/2.r on the other, so I placed the button to match the card. Side 1 = 't' half (columns 4 and 6), side 2 = 'b' half. The pin-2 wire and resistor are on side 1 and the 5V wire is on side 2, so the pull-down works as the text describes.

Hole positions are approximated from the image (it is drawn flipped relative to the catalogue's row naming). The rail used is the one beside the a-e rows, which is tp/tn in the catalogue. The rail's upper line is - (tn) and its lower red line is + (tp).

The 10k resistor runs from column 6 to column 9 on row c. The short black wire joins column 9 (row b) to the - rail. The orange wire is placed on the 'b' half of column 4 and runs to the + rail so it reaches the other button side.
